note: Spec process rewritten after STP-4: frame first, questions before text, short criteria, one ordered spec review, summary confirmation, code review without quotas, escaped defects as the main measure, rules pruned after three tickets without a catch. STP-5 is the pilot. The six narrow fixes from the STP-4 retrospective are folded into items 1 to 4 and 6.

Builder pilot on STP-5 R1: a 1200-token brief was enough for a context-free Sonnet builder; it read 0.93M cache tokens in 17 calls against about 3.9M per orchestrator step; the orchestrator's 650k-token context per call is the main cost. Next: start each ticket in a new session; phase 1 coordination by stapel.

Builder briefs need explicit history rules: a GREEN changes nothing under tests; a coverage commit only adds #[test] functions with nested helpers; a test changed by a new rule is changed only in a RED; the orchestrator runs stapel check after every builder commit. Code review found that PostToolUse does not fire after a Bash call that exits non-zero (PostToolUseFailure does), so the commit hook missed the usual builder form `git commit … && cargo test`. The claude-code dimensions of external-states.yml have no row for tool success or failure; candidate row: claude-code "tool call succeeded or failed (PostToolUse versus PostToolUseFailure)".

The orchestrator broke its own rules three times: an uncommitted edit of ticket.md during the build made design stale and the guard stopped a builder; a plain commit changed the test helper fixtures.rs, which the full check reads as build-input-changed, so the human rewrote history; `stapel ok` behind a pipe or a redirection is not read by the guard, so no dialog appeared. A step 2 test held `someone@example.invalid`, which only the full suite (fixtures) caught: builder briefs should also run `--test fixtures` before GREEN.
